1-5.word_for_word: tṛtīye — in the third chapter; nija-rūpeṇa — in His own form; sambhūtaḥ tu hariḥ svayam — Hari Himself appeared; pitṛbhyām saṁstutaḥ — praised by His two parents; pitrā bhītena gokulam nītaḥ — taken to Gokula by His frightened father; atha — the word ‘atha’; maṅgala-artham — for auspiciousness; yarhi sarva-guṇa-upetaḥ kālaḥ babhūva — when the time became endowed with every excellence; tadā devakyām viṣṇuḥ āvirāsīt — then Viṣṇu appeared in Devakī; aṣṭama-śloka-gatena anvayaḥ — the syntactic completion occurs in verse 8; ajanāt nārāyaṇāt janma yasya prajāpateḥ tasya ṛkṣam — the constellation of the Prajāpati born from the unborn Nārāyaṇa; rohiṇī-nakṣatram — the constellation Rohiṇī; śāntāni ṛkṣāṇi — the constellations were peaceful; grahāḥ ca tārakāḥ ca — the planets and stars also; nirmalānām uḍu-gaṇānām udayaḥ — the rising of spotless hosts of stars; maṅgala-bhūyiṣṭhāḥ purādayaḥ — the cities and other settlements were exceedingly auspicious; jalaruhaiḥ śrīḥ śobhā — beauty through the lotuses; dvijāli-kulānām pakṣi-bhṛṅga-samūhānām sannādaḥ — the resounding of groups of birds and swarms of bees; samindhata — they blazed; samyag dīptā babhūvuḥ — they became brightly kindled; asura-druhām — of those opposed to the demons; kaṁsādi-vyatiriktānām sarva-prāṇinām devānām ca — of all living beings other than Kaṁsa and the other demons, and of the gods; ajane jāyamāne — when the unborn Lord was being born.
1-5.translation: In the third chapter Hari Himself appears in His own form, is praised by His parents, and is carried to Gokula by His frightened father. ‘Atha’ is used for auspiciousness. The syntax is: when the time became endowed with every excellence, Viṣṇu appeared in Devakī, as stated in verse 8. The text then explains why that time was supremely beautiful. The constellation belonging to the Prajāpati born from the unborn Nārāyaṇa is Rohiṇī; the constellations, planets and stars were peaceful. The sky shone with spotless hosts of stars, the cities and other settlements of the earth were exceedingly auspicious, the lakes were beautiful with lotuses, and the forests resounded with groups of birds and swarms of bees. ‘Samindhata’ means that the sacrificial fires blazed brightly. ‘Those opposed to the demons’ means all living beings other than Kaṁsa and the other demons, and also the gods. The words about the birthless Lord being born introduce what especially occurred in heaven.

6.word_for_word: tadā — then; āsannaḥ prasavaḥ — the appearance or birth was near; yasmin tasmin samaye — at that time.
6.translation: This occurred at the time when the Lord’s appearance was near.

7-8.word_for_word: anusāgaram — following or imitating the ocean; sāgara-nādam anulakṣya — in imitation of the ocean’s sound; mandam jagarja — the clouds rumbled softly; tamasā udbhūte — when darkness had arisen; ghana-tamasi niśīthe — in the dense darkness of midnight; yathā — exactly as He is; yathāvat aiśvareṇa eva rūpeṇa — in His very divine form.
7-8.translation: ‘Anusāgaram’ means that the clouds rumbled softly in imitation of the ocean’s sound. ‘When darkness had arisen’ means in the dense darkness of midnight. The comparison beginning with ‘yathā’ indicates that the Lord appeared exactly as He is, in His own divine form.

9-10.word_for_word: tam adbhutam bālakam vasudevaḥ aikṣata — Vasudeva saw that wondrous child; dvitīya-ślokena anvayaḥ — the construction is completed by the second of the two verses; adbhutatve hetu-garbhāṇi viśeṣaṇāni — the adjectives contain the reasons for His wondrousness; ambuja-īkṣaṇam ity-ādīni — beginning with ‘lotus-eyed’; śrīvatsa-lakṣmam — bearing the Śrīvatsa mark; gala-śobhī sa kaustubhaḥ yasmin — in whom the Kaustubha jewel beautified the neck; pariṣvakta-sahasra-kuntalam — whose innumerable locks were embraced by radiance; kirīṭa-kuṇḍalādīnām tviṣā — by the brilliance of the crown, earrings and other ornaments; sphurat-aparimita-keśam — with countless gleaming locks.
9-10.translation: The construction completed in the second verse is: ‘Vasudeva saw that wondrous child.’ The descriptions beginning with ‘lotus-eyed’ explain why He was wondrous. ‘Śrīvatsa-lakṣmam’ means bearing the mark of Śrīvatsa. ‘Gala-śobhi-kaustubham’ means that the Kaustubha jewel shone upon His neck. ‘Pariṣvakta-sahasra-kuntalam’ means that His innumerable locks gleamed, embraced by the radiance of His crown, earrings and other ornaments.

11.word_for_word: vismayena utphulle vikasite locane yasya — whose eyes opened wide in wonder; gavām ayutam aspṛśat — he ‘touched’ ten thousand cows; manasā dattavān — he gave them mentally; kaṁsa-nigṛhītasya dāna-asambhavāt — because an actual gift was impossible for one imprisoned by Kaṁsa; kṛṣṇa-avatāra-utsava — the festival of Kṛṣṇa’s appearance; mudā āplutaḥ — flooded with joy; snātaḥ iti vā — or, ‘having bathed.’
11.translation: His eyes were opened wide in wonder. ‘He touched ten thousand cows’ means that he mentally gave them away, since, being imprisoned by Kaṁsa, an actual gift was impossible. The reason for making the gift was the festival of Kṛṣṇa’s appearance. ‘Āplutaḥ’ may mean overwhelmed with joy, or bathed.

12.word_for_word: kṛta-dhīḥ — one whose understanding is purified; śuddha-buddhiḥ — of pure intelligence.
12.translation: ‘Kṛta-dhīḥ’ means one whose understanding had become purified.

13.word_for_word: vasudevaḥ prathamam putra-buddhyā paśyan — Vasudeva at first saw Him with the conception ‘my son’; tām parityajya — setting that conception aside; viditaḥ asi — ‘You are known by me’; bhavān prakṛteḥ paraḥ puruṣaḥ — You are the Person beyond material nature; sākṣāt — directly, before the eyes; kevalaḥ anubhavaḥ ca ānandaḥ ca svarūpam yasya — whose very nature is pure consciousness or experience and bliss; sarva-buddhi-dṛk — the witness of every intellect; na hi evaṁ-bhūtaḥ dṛśyaḥ bhavati — one of such a nature is not ordinarily an object of sight.
13.translation: Seeing Him at first simply as his son, Vasudeva set that conception aside and said, ‘I know You.’ He knows Him as the Person beyond material nature and, astonishingly, directly present before his eyes. The Lord’s very nature is pure consciousness and bliss, and He is the witness of every intellect. One of such a nature is ordinarily not an object of sight.

14.word_for_word: devakī-jaṭhare praviṣṭasya kim iyam ati-stutiḥ — why such excessive praise of One who has entered Devakī’s womb?; sa eva ukta-svarūpaḥ eva tvam — You remain exactly the Reality just described; na devakī-jaṭhare praviṣṭaḥ — You have not literally entered Devakī’s belly; sva-prakṛtyā — through Your own prakṛti, Your own māyā; sṛṣṭvā — having created; tad anu tvam apraviṣṭaḥ eva — even afterward You remain unentered; praviṣṭa iva — as if entered; bhāvyase — You are described or contemplated; pratyakṣataḥ vā sat-rūpeṇa vā — perceptibly, or as Being itself; praviṣṭa iva lakṣyase — You appear as though entered.
14.translation: If one asks why such praise is offered to One who has entered Devakī’s womb, the answer is that You remain exactly the Reality just described: You have not literally entered her womb. Even after creating the universe through Your own māyā, You remain unentered. Scripture therefore says You are ‘as if entered’: You are described or perceived as though entering, although You are already present as Being itself.

15-17.word_for_word: atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ — here an analogy is given; ime avikṛtā bhāvā mahad-ādayaḥ — these unmodified principles beginning with mahat; vikṛtaiḥ ṣoḍaśa-vikāraiḥ saha — together with the sixteen transformations; sannipatya — joining together; virājam brahmāṇḍam janayanti — produce the Virāṭ, the cosmic egg; pṛthag-bhūtāḥ — remaining separate; viśiṣṭa-kārya-samarthā na bhavanti — they are not capable of that particular work; samutpādya anugatāḥ praviṣṭā iva dṛśyante — after producing it they appear to have entered it; na punaḥ praviṣṭāḥ — but they did not subsequently enter; utpatteḥ prāk eva kāraṇatayā vidyamānatvāt — because they already existed beforehand as causes; evaṁ bhavān — so it is with You; buddhy-anumeya-lakṣaṇaiḥ grāhyaiḥ guṇaiḥ saha san api — although present together with qualities whose forms are inferred by cognition and grasped by the senses; taiḥ guṇaiḥ saha na gṛhyate — You are not grasped along with those qualities; na hi grāhyaiḥ saha bhāva-mātram grahaṇe kāraṇam — mere coexistence with perceptible things is not a sufficient cause of perception; indriyāṇām śaktiḥ — the specific power of each sense; yathā cakṣuṣā rūpa-grahaṇe rasādi-grahaṇam nāsti — as the eye grasps form but not taste; anāvṛtatvāt — because You are unenclosed and unlimited; bahir-antar-bhedaḥ na asti — there is no distinction of inside and outside; sarvasya — because You are the form of all; sarvātmanaḥ — the Self of all; ātma-vastunaḥ — the all-pervading Self and true Reality; tavāntaryāmitayā praveśaḥ na mukhyaḥ — even Your indwelling is not literal spatial entry; kutaḥ tarām garbhe praveśaḥ — much less an entry into a womb.
15-17.translation: Here an analogy is given. The unmodified principles beginning with mahat join with the sixteen transformations and produce the Virāṭ, the cosmic egg. Separate from one another they cannot perform that particular work, so they combine. After producing it they appear to have entered it, but they did not enter afterward, because they were already present beforehand as its causes. The example is then applied to the Lord. Although You are present together with qualities perceptible to the senses, those qualities do not make You an object grasped by the senses. Mere coexistence with something perceptible is not sufficient for perception; each sense has only its own power, just as the eye grasps form but not taste. Since You are not an object of the senses, they cannot apprehend You. Moreover, because You are unlimited there is no division of inside and outside for You. As the Self of all and the truly existing Reality, nothing can enclose You. Thus even Your indwelling is not a literal spatial entry—much less an entry into a womb.

18.word_for_word: ātmano dṛśyeṣu guṇeṣu dehādiṣu — among visible attributes such as the body; sva-vyatirekataḥ — as separate from the Self; ayam dehādiḥ pṛthak san iti vyavasyate — one determines that body and the rest exist independently; saḥ abudhaḥ avidvān — that person is ignorant; manīṣitam vicāritam — when examined by thought; dehādi sarvam — the body and all such things; vinā anuvādam vācārambhaṇa-mātram vinā — apart from mere verbal designation; na samyak bhavati — does not stand independently; avastutvena tyaktam bādhitam — negated as non-independent reality; vastu-buddhyā upādadat — nevertheless accepted as substantial; abudhaḥ — ignorant.
18.translation: One who determines that the visible qualities such as the body exist independently, apart from the Self, is ignorant. When examined, body and the rest do not stand as independent realities apart from verbal designation. Therefore one who accepts as substantial what has been negated as non-independent is ignorant.

19.word_for_word: parameśvara-dṛśyasya tad-vyatirekeṇa asattvam — the visible universe has no existence apart from the Supreme Lord; parameśvara-upādānatvāt — because the Supreme Lord is its underlying material basis; anīhāt — from the actionless One; aguṇatvāt anīhatvam — actionlessness follows from being beyond the guṇas; tataḥ avikāritvam — therefore changelessness; brahmatvāt avikāritvam — changelessness because He is Brahman; īśvaratvāt kartṛtvam — agency because He is the Lord; tvad-āśrayatvāt — because the guṇas rest upon You; guṇaiḥ kurvadbhiḥ tvayi sṛṣṭy-ādi-kartṛtvam upacaryate — creation and other acts performed by the guṇas are figuratively attributed to You; yathā bhṛtya-kṛtyam rājanītiḥ — just as the servants’ deeds are spoken of as the king’s policy.
19.translation: The visible universe has no existence apart from the Supreme Lord, both because He is its underlying basis and because it depends upon Him. Yet He does not undergo transformation: being beyond the guṇas He is actionless, and therefore changeless. How then can agency belong to Him? As Brahman He is changeless; as Īśvara He is the ruler. Creation and the other acts are figuratively attributed to Him because the acting guṇas rest upon Him—just as the deeds of servants are spoken of as the king’s policy.

20.word_for_word: evaṁ-bhūtasya tava — of You, who are of this nature; viśva-sthiti-sarga-pralaya-artham — for maintenance, creation and dissolution of the universe; tri-varṇā guṇa-avatārāḥ — the three-colored incarnations associated with the guṇas; evam ayam — so also this present descent; bhū-bhāra-apanayana-artham — for removing the burden of the earth; iti jñātam — is thus understood; sa tvam iti śloka-dvayena — by this verse and the next.
20.translation: Just as Your three-colored guṇa-avatāras function for the maintenance, creation and dissolution of the universe, this present descent is understood to be for removing the burden of the earth. This is explained in this verse and the next.

21.word_for_word: rirakṣiṣuḥ — desiring to protect; rakṣitum icchuḥ avatīrṇaḥ asi — You have descended wishing to protect; kṛṣṇena varṇena — in the dark-hued form; sādhūnām rakṣaṇa-artham — for protecting the righteous; rājanya-saṁjñāḥ — those bearing the designation of kings; asura-koṭi-yūthapāḥ — leaders of hordes of demons; taiḥ nirvyūhyamānāḥ — driven and maneuvered here and there by them; camūḥ senāḥ — the armies; nihaniṣyase saṁhariṣyasi — You will destroy them.
21.translation: You have descended in the dark-hued form desiring to protect. For the protection of the righteous You will destroy the armies, driven here and there by leaders of hordes of demons who bear the name of kings.

22.word_for_word: tathā api apramattena tvayā bhāvyam — even so, You should remain alert; asabhyaḥ — uncivilized, wicked; khalaḥ — a villain; samarpitam — reported, told; abhisarati — he approaches; āgamiṣyati — he will come.
22.translation: Still, You should remain alert. ‘Asabhyaḥ’ means this Kaṁsa is a wicked man; ‘samarpitam’ means reported to him; and ‘abhisarati’ means that he will come at once.

23.word_for_word: upādhāvat — she approached; astaut — she praised Him.
23.translation: ‘She approached Him’ means that she praised Him.

24.word_for_word: tvayi bhaya-śaṅkā eva na asti — in You there is no possibility of fear; devakī kiñcid vijñāpayitum — Devakī, wishing to make a request; yat tat rūpam vastu prāhuḥ vedāḥ — that Reality whose nature the Vedas declare; avyaktam — unmanifest; ādyam — primal, the cause; brahma — the unlimited; jyotiḥ — self-luminous consciousness; nirguṇam — beyond qualities; nirvikāram — without transformation; sattā-mātram — pure Being; nirviśeṣam — without limiting differentiation; nirīham — actionless; sannidhi-mātreṇa kāraṇam — a cause by mere presence; sa eva sākṣāt tvam viṣṇuḥ — that very Reality is directly You, Viṣṇu; adhyātma-dīpaḥ — the light of the inner self; buddhy-ādi-karaṇa-saṅghāta-prakāśakaḥ — the illuminator of the complex of intellect and the other inner instruments; na kenāpi prakāreṇa vyajyate — not manifested by any external means; sarvasya kāryasya ādyam, anādi — prior to every effect and beginningless; deśena prakāśena guṇena vikāreṇa ca vyaktim nirākaroti — manifestation through place, light, quality or transformation is denied; viśeṣeṇa sāmānyena kriyayā ca vyaktim nirākaroti — manifestation through particularity, generic class or action is also denied.
24.translation: Devakī, wishing to make a request, first declares that fear cannot truly apply to Him. The Vedas speak of that Reality as unmanifest, because it is the primal cause; as Brahman, because it is unlimited; as light, because it is conscious; as beyond qualities and transformation; as pure Being; as without limiting differentiation; and as actionless, causing things merely by its presence. That very Reality is directly You, Viṣṇu. ‘Adhyātma-dīpa’ means the light that illumines the complex of intellect and the other inner instruments. Alternatively, ‘unmanifest’ means not manifested by any external means. Being beginningless, unlimited, self-luminous, beyond qualities and change, pure Being, without limiting differentiation and inactive, it cannot be made manifest by place, light, quality, transformation, particularity, generic class or action. Therefore fear has no possible footing in One of this nature.

25.word_for_word: mahā-pralaye api avaśiṣyamāṇasya kutaḥ bhayam — how could there be fear for One who remains even at the great dissolution?; carācare loke naṣṭe — when the moving and unmoving world is destroyed; mahā-bhūteṣu līneṣu — when the gross elements have dissolved; ādi-bhūtam bhūta-sūkṣmam praviṣṭeṣu — when they have entered their subtle cause; vyakte avyaktaṁ pradhānam prāpte — when the manifest has reached the unmanifest pradhāna; aśeṣa-saṁjñaḥ — possessing awareness regarding the totality; evaṁ mayi līnam idam asti — ‘all this lies dissolved in Me’; paścāt evam udbodhanīyam — ‘later it is to be awakened again’; śeṣa-saṁjñaḥ iti vā — or the reading may be ‘known as Śeṣa.’
25.translation: How could there be fear for One who remains even at the great dissolution? When the moving and unmoving world is destroyed, when the gross elements have merged into their subtle cause, and that manifest principle has entered the unmanifest pradhāna, You alone remain. ‘Aśeṣa-saṁjña’ can mean the One whose awareness remains with respect to the totality dissolved within pradhāna—knowing, ‘All this lies dissolved in Me and will later be awakened again.’ The reading may also be understood as ‘Śeṣa-saṁjña,’ the One known as Śeṣa.

26.word_for_word: pralaya-hetuḥ yaḥ ayam kālaḥ — this time which is the cause of dissolution; he avyakta-bandho — O mover or master of the unmanifest prakṛti; tasya te ceṣṭām līlām — it is Your movement or play; nimeṣa-ādiḥ vatsara-antaḥ — beginning with a blink and extending through a year; punaḥ punaḥ vatsara-āvṛttyā — turning again and again through recurring years; mahīyān dvi-parārdha-rūpaḥ — on the greatest scale extending through two parārdhas; yasya ceṣṭām āhuḥ tam tvām — You whose activity they call time; kṣema-dhāma — abode of safety, fearlessness; prapadye — I take refuge.
26.translation: The time that causes dissolution itself is described as Your movement or play, O mover of prakṛti. Beginning with a blink and extending through the year, it turns again and again and, on the greatest scale, extends through two parārdhas. You are the Lord whose activity time is said to be; I therefore take refuge in You as the abode of fearlessness.

27.word_for_word: kṣema-dhāmatvam eva āha — this explains His being the abode of safety; martyaḥ mṛtyu-vyāla-bhītaḥ — a mortal terrified by the serpent of death; lokān prati palāyan — fleeing through the worlds; nirbhayam na adhyagacchat — found no place free of fear; yadṛcchayā — by chance, through some arising of good fortune; kenāpi bhāgya-udayena — through the rise of some good fortune; tvat-pādābjam prāpya — reaching Your lotus feet; he ādya — O Primal One; susthaḥ śete — he rests secure; mṛtyuḥ asmāt apaiti — death withdraws from him.
27.translation: This explains why He is the abode of safety. A mortal, fleeing through all worlds in fear of the serpent of death, finds no fearlessness; but by some arising of good fortune he reaches Your lotus feet, O Primal One, rests secure, and death withdraws from him.

28.word_for_word: prastutam vijñāpayati — she now states her actual request; bhṛtyānām vitrāsam hanti — He destroys the terror of His servants; bhṛtya-vitrāsa-hā — destroyer of His servants’ fear; pauruṣam — divine, sovereign; aiśvaram — belonging to divine majesty; dhyāna-dhiṣṇyam — the seat or object of meditation; māṁsa-dṛśām — of those whose eyes are merely flesh; māṁsa-cakṣuṣām — fleshly eyes; pratyakṣam mā kṛthāḥ — do not make it directly visible.
28.translation: She now states her actual request: You destroy the terror of Your servants. ‘Pauruṣam’ means this divine sovereign form; ‘dhyāna-dhiṣṇyam,’ the object of meditation; ‘māṁsa-dṛśām,’ those whose eyes are only flesh. Do not make this form visible to such eyes.

29.word_for_word: bhavataḥ eva hetoḥ — precisely because of You, for Your sake; kaṁsāt samudvije — I tremble before Kaṁsa; bibhemi — I fear; yataḥ adhīra-cittā — because my mind is unsteady with maternal affection.
29.translation: It is precisely because of You that I tremble before Kaṁsa: I fear for Your sake, because a mother’s mind is unsteady with affection.

31.word_for_word: kim iti upasaṁhartavyam — why should this form be withdrawn?; evaṁ-bhūtena mayā putreṇa tava mahatī ślāghā syāt — with such a son you would have immense praise; viśvam iti — she answers with the verse beginning ‘the universe’; niśānte — at the end of the cosmic night, at dissolution; pralayāvasāne — at the end of dissolution; yathāvakāśam — according to the available space, without contraction; asaṅkocataḥ — without becoming contracted; asambhāvitatvāt — because such a claim would seem impossible; upahāsyatā eva syāt — it would instead become a cause of ridicule.
31.translation: If one asks why this form should be withdrawn—would not having such a son bring you immense fame?—Devakī answers with ‘this universe.’ At the end of the cosmic night He bears the universe within Himself without contraction. To say that this very Person entered my womb would seem impossible to ordinary people and would only make me an object of ridicule.

32.word_for_word: catur-bhujena rūpeṇa āvirbhāve kāraṇam — the reason for appearing in the four-armed form; tvam eva ity-ādi caturdaśabhiḥ — explained in the fourteen verses beginning ‘you indeed’; pūrva-sarge — in the previous creation; prathama-janmani — in the first birth; abhūḥ āsīḥ — you were; pṛśniḥ nāma — named Pṛśni; svāyambhuve manvantare — in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara; tadā ayam vasudevaḥ — the present Vasudeva was then Sutapā.
32.translation: He first explains why He appeared in the four-armed form, in the fourteen verses beginning here. ‘In the previous creation’ means in their first birth. In the Svāyambhuva Manvantara you were named Pṛśni, and the present Vasudeva was then the Prajāpati Sutapā.

33.word_for_word: tepāthe — the two of you performed; tapaḥ kṛtavantau — you performed austerity.
33.translation: ‘Tepāthe’ means that the two of you performed austerity.

34-35.word_for_word: īhatuḥ — the two of them undertook or carried out; kṛtavantau — they performed it; mad-ārādhanam — My worship; upaśāntena cetasā — with a pacified mind.
34-35.translation: ‘Īhatuḥ’ means that the two of them carried out this effort of worshiping Me with pacified minds.

36.word_for_word: tapyatoḥ — as the two of you practiced austerity; ācaratoḥ — while performing it; īyuḥ — they went, they passed; gatāni — elapsed; divya-varṣa-sahasrāṇi — thousands of celestial years; mad-ātmanoḥ — of those whose minds were in Me; mat-cittayoḥ — whose thoughts were fixed on Me.
36.translation: ‘As you were performing austerity’ means while practicing it; ‘īyuḥ’ means that the years passed; and ‘mad-ātmanoḥ’ means that both of your minds were fixed on Me.

37-38.word_for_word: amunā vapuṣā — with this very form; prādurbhūtaḥ asmi — I appeared; varada-rāṭ — king of boon-givers; varadeṣu śreṣṭhaḥ — foremost among those who grant boons; sakṛt-vareṇa — by a single boon; vāram vāram āvirbhāve kāraṇam — the cause of repeated appearances; kāmasya ditsayā — from the desire to grant your wish; dātum icchayā — wishing to give it; mādṛśaḥ — one like Me; mayā sadṛśaḥ — resembling Me.
37-38.translation: ‘With this very form’ means that I appeared to you in this form. ‘Varada-rāṭ’ means the foremost among givers of boons; thus a single boon became the cause of My appearing again and again. ‘Kāmasya ditsayā’ means from the desire to grant your wish, and ‘mādṛśaḥ’ means a son like Me.

39.word_for_word: me — from Me; mattaḥ api — even from Me; yuvām — the two of you; apavargam na vavrāthe — did not choose liberation; na vṛtavantau — you did not select it.
39.translation: Even from Me, the giver of the boon, the two of you did not choose liberation.

40.word_for_word: varam dattvā — having granted the boon; mayi gate — when I had departed.
40.translation: The sense is: after I had granted the boon and departed.

42.word_for_word: adityām kaśyapāt vāmanaḥ āsa — Vāmana was born from Kaśyapa in Aditi; iti yat — that statement; tad api — that also; tad-rūpayoḥ yuvayoḥ — of the same two of you in those forms; aham eva punaḥ āsam — I Myself again became their son.
42.translation: The statement that Vāmana was born from Kaśyapa in Aditi means that I Myself again became the son of the same two of you in those forms.

44.word_for_word: prāk — first, beforehand; etad rūpam me — this form of Mine; janma iti smaraṇāya — for remembrance of My former birth or appearance; jñānāya — for recognition; darśitam — was shown; mad-bhavam — concerning Me; anantaram — afterward; tvad-icchayā — according to your wish; bālaḥ api bhaviṣyāmi — I will also become an ordinary child.
44.translation: First this form of Mine was shown so that you might remember and recognize My former appearance. ‘Mad-bhavam’ means knowledge concerning Me. The implication is that afterward, in accordance with your wish, I will also appear as an ordinary child.

45.word_for_word: nanu tvayi prasanne api — although You were pleased with us; katham āvayoḥ punaḥ punaḥ janma — why did the two of us have repeated births?; ataḥ param na bhaviṣyati — after this there will be no further birth; yuvām iti — this is stated in the verse beginning ‘you two.’
45.translation: If one asks, ‘Although You were pleased with us, why did we have to take birth again and again?’ the Lord answers that there will be no further birth after this.

47.word_for_word: yadi kaṁsāt bibheṣi — if you fear Kaṁsa; tarhi mām gokulam naya — then take Me to Gokula; yaśodāyāḥ ca tām kanyām — and Yaśodā’s daughter; mat-māyām ānaya — bring back My māyā; prathamam eva bhagavatā pracoditaḥ vasudevaḥ — Vasudeva had already been instructed by Bhagavān; yadā gantum aicchat — when he wished to depart; tadā eva ajā api yā yoga-māyā — at that very time the unborn Yogamāyā; nanda-jāyayā nimitta-mātra-bhūtayā — with Nanda’s wife serving merely as the immediate instrumental mother; ajani jātā — was born.
47.translation: The Lord had already instructed Vasudeva: ‘If you fear Kaṁsa, take Me to Gokula and bring back Yaśodā’s daughter, My māyā.’ When Vasudeva then intended to leave, the unborn Yogamāyā was born, with Nanda’s wife serving as the immediate instrumental mother.

48-49.word_for_word: hṛtāḥ pratyaya-arthāḥ sarvā vṛttayaḥ yeṣām — those whose every mental function relating to cognition had been taken away; athavā hṛtāḥ pratyayāḥ anyāḥ ca sarvāḥ vṛttayaḥ — alternatively, their cognitions and all other mental functions had been removed; jāgratām api dvāra-pāleṣu — even from the guards who had been awake; bṛhatsu kapāṭeṣu — in the massive doors; loha-kīlaka-yukta-śṛṅkhalaiḥ — with chains fitted with iron bolts; duratyayāḥ — impossible to cross; svayam eva vyavaryanta — they opened by themselves; vivṛtāḥ — they became open; vyavriyanta iti vaktavye — the expected form would be ‘vyavriyanta’; guṇaḥ chāndasaḥ — the form in the verse is Vedic; raveḥ nimittāt — on account of the sun, i.e. like darkness before the sun.
48-49.translation: The guards had their cognitions and all other mental functions removed; thus even those who had been awake were reduced to helpless sleep. The doors were ordinarily impossible to cross because of their massive panels, iron bolts and chains. Yet they opened by themselves. The expected verbal form is ‘vyavriyanta’; the form in the verse is Vedic. The comparison with darkness before the sun indicates that the doors opened of themselves before Kṛṣṇa’s arrival.

50.word_for_word: gambhīraḥ yaḥ toya-oghaḥ — the deep mass of water; tasya javena — by its force; ye ūrmayaḥ — the waves; taiḥ phenilā — made foamy by them; phena-vyāptā — covered with foam; bhayānakaiḥ āvarta-śataiḥ vyāptā api — though filled with hundreds of terrifying whirlpools; śriyaḥ pateḥ — of the Lord of Śrī; sītā-pateḥ — of Sītā’s Lord, Rāma.
50.translation: The river was covered with foam from the waves driven by the force of its deep flood, and filled with hundreds of terrifying whirlpools. ‘The Lord of Śrī’ here refers to Sītā’s Lord, Rāma, for whom the ocean had once given a path.

51.word_for_word: nidrayā — by sleep; ajayā — by Ajā, the unborn Yogamāyā.
51.translation: ‘By sleep’ means by Ajā, the unborn Yogamāyā.

52.word_for_word: pratimucya — fastening or binding again; vaddhvā — having bound; padoḥ — on the two feet; pādayoḥ — upon his feet; loham — the iron; nigaḍam — shackle; āste sma — he remained there as before.
52.translation: ‘Pratimucya’ means binding again; ‘padoḥ,’ upon his feet; ‘loham,’ the iron shackle; and ‘āste,’ he remained there as before.

53.word_for_word: jātam kiñcid iti kevalam abudhyata — she understood only that some child had been born; na tu tat-liṅgam — but not its distinguishing sign; putraḥ kanyā vā iti — whether it was a son or a daughter; yoga-nidrayā ca mohitā — she had also been bewildered by Yogamāyā’s sleep.
53.translation: She understood only that some child had been born; she did not know the distinguishing sign—whether it was a son or a daughter—for she had also been bewildered by Yogamāyā’s sleep.
